tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

=== README.md
# towtank-drag

Drag on smooth circular cylinders towed through the tank. 1in, 2in and
1.5in cylinders, 0.6 m submerged.

## Processing

1. `python process.py` (change DATA path to wherever the raw data is)
2. `python process_b3.py` for the March data (new DAQ format)
3. run `analysis.ipynb` -> Cd vs Re plot in figures/

`plot_timeseries.py` makes the example trace figure.

Calibration files are in data/calibration. Run log is data/run_log.csv.

old_matlab/ is Jamie's original processing script, kept for reference.

=== process.py
# process tow tank runs -> mean drag force for each run
import glob
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA = "/Users/mkim/Dropbox/towtank/data/raw"
BATCHES = ["2025-10-14", "2025-11-03"]

cal = pd.read_csv("data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv")
sens = np.polyfit(cal.mass_g / 1000 * 9.81, cal.voltage_V, 1)[0]  # V/N
print("sensitivity", sens)

rows = []
for b in BATCHES:
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(DATA, b, "run_*.csv"))):
        d = pd.read_csv(f, comment="#")
        tare = d.loadcell_V[d.time_s < 1.0].mean()
        F = (d.loadcell_V - tare) / sens
        steady = (d.time_s > 3) & (d.time_s < 8)
        rows.append({
            "run": int(os.path.basename(f)[4:7]),
            "F_mean": F[steady].mean(),
            "F_std": F[steady].std(),
        })

out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out.to_csv("processed/forces.csv", index=False)
print("done", len(out))

=== old_matlab/towtank_proc.m
% towtank_proc.m  - J. Rivera, 2024
% mean drag from one run file. usage: F = towtank_proc('run_001.csv', 0.02)
function F = towtank_proc(fname, sens)
    d = readmatrix(fname, 'NumHeaderLines', 3);
    t = d(:,1); v = d(:,2);
    tare = mean(v(t < 1));
    f = (v - tare) / sens;
    F = mean(f(t > 3 & t < 8));
end

=== README.md
# towtank-drag

Drag on smooth circular cylinders towed through the tank. 1in, 2in and
1.5in cylinders, 0.6 m submerged.

## Processing

1. `python process.py` (change DATA path to wherever the raw data is)
2. `python process_b3.py` for the March data (new DAQ format)
3. run `analysis.ipynb` -> Cd vs Re plot in figures/

`plot_timeseries.py` makes the example trace figure.

Calibration files are in data/calibration. Run log is data/run_log.csv.

old_matlab/ is Jamie's original processing script, kept for reference.
=== notes.md
# towtank notes

2025-09-30  calibrated load cell (data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv),
            sens ~0.020 V/N

2025-10-14  1in cylinder, 10 speeds 0.2-1.1 m/s. water ~17C

            (drift?) - recheck or toss

            DAQ software updated -> new file format (semicolons)

2026-03-12  1.5in cylinder, 10 speeds. water cold (~14C)

2026-03-20  wrote process_b3.py for the new format, added to notebook

=== requirements.txt

=== process.py
# process tow tank runs -> mean drag force for each run
import glob
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA = "/Users/mkim/Dropbox/towtank/data/raw"
BATCHES = ["2025-10-14", "2025-11-03"]

cal = pd.read_csv("data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv")
sens = np.polyfit(cal.mass_g / 1000 * 9.81, cal.voltage_V, 1)[0]  # V/N
print("sensitivity", sens)

rows = []
for b in BATCHES:
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(DATA, b, "run_*.csv"))):
        d = pd.read_csv(f, comment="#")
        tare = d.loadcell_V[d.time_s < 1.0].mean()
        F = (d.loadcell_V - tare) / sens
        steady = (d.time_s > 3) & (d.time_s < 8)
        rows.append({
            "run": int(os.path.basename(f)[4:7]),
            "F_mean": F[steady].mean(),
            "F_std": F[steady].std(),
        })

out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out.to_csv("processed/forces.csv", index=False)
print("done", len(out))

=== old_matlab/towtank_proc.m
% towtank_proc.m  - J. Rivera, 2024
% mean drag from one run file. usage: F = towtank_proc('run_001.csv', 0.02)
function F = towtank_proc(fname, sens)
    d = readmatrix(fname, 'NumHeaderLines', 3);
    t = d(:,1); v = d(:,2);
    tare = mean(v(t < 1));
    f = (v - tare) / sens;
    F = mean(f(t > 3 & t < 8));
end

import glob, os, numpy as np, pandas as pd
for f in sorted(glob.glob('data/calibration/*.csv')):
    c=pd.read_csv(f); x=c.mass_g/1000*9.81; p=np.polyfit(x,c.voltage_V,1)
    print(f, 'sens %.5f V/N off %.5f maxresid %.2e'%(p[0],p[1],abs(c.voltage_V-np.polyval(p,x)).max()))
for f in sorted(glob.glob('data/raw/*/run_*.csv')):
    try: d=pd.read_csv(f,comment='#'); t,v=d.iloc[:,0],d.iloc[:,1]
    except Exception: d=pd.read_csv(f,sep=';'); t,v=d.t,d.V
    if t.shape[0]<5 or 'V' not in d.columns and 'loadcell_V' not in d.columns:
        d=pd.read_csv(f,sep=';'); t,v=d.t,d.V
    print(os.path.basename(f), len(t), 'dt %.4f T %.2f'%(t.diff().median(), t.iloc[-1]), 'pre %.5f post %.5f steady %.5f'%(v[t<1].mean(), v[t>t.iloc[-1]-1].mean(), v[(t>3)&(t<8)].mean()))
EOF
uv run --no-project --with pandas --with numpy python -I /tmp/towscratch/check.py 2>&1 | grep -v Install

Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/agent-runs/dev/tmpfy2drkdi/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.310/1a322d887c97663cbb65c77eaa365935/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

# process tow tank runs -> mean drag force for each run
#
# Handles both DAQ file formats (v2.1 comma-separated with "#" header, and the
# March 2026 semicolon format), picks the load cell calibration in effect on
# the run date, and flags runs whose zero drifted during the tow.
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import signal

RAW = "data/raw"
FS = 200.0  # Hz
TARE_WINDOW = (0.0, 1.0)  # s, carriage at rest before the tow
STEADY_WINDOW = (3.0, 8.0)  # s, constant-speed part of the tow
POST_WINDOW = 1.0  # s, last part of the record, carriage at rest again
BLOCK_S = 0.5  # s, block length for the random uncertainty of the mean
MAX_ZERO_DRIFT_N = 0.05  # N, |post-run zero - pre-run tare| above this -> excluded

# Calibration in effect from each date (load cell remounted 2026-03-10)
CALIBRATIONS = [
    ("2025-09-30", "data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv"),
    ("2026-03-10", "data/calibration/loadcell_2026-03.csv"),
]


def fit_calibration(path):
    """Linear fit of voltage vs applied force; returns slope (V/N) and its std error."""
    cal = pd.read_csv(path)
    force = cal.mass_g / 1000 * 9.81
    p, cov = np.polyfit(force, cal.voltage_V, 1, cov=True)
    return p[0], np.sqrt(cov[0, 0])


def calibration_for(date):
    valid = [c for c in CALIBRATIONS if c[0] <= date]
    return valid[-1][1]


def read_run(path):
    """Return time (s) and load cell voltage (V) for either DAQ file format."""
    with open(path) as f:
        first = f.readline()
    if first.startswith("#"):
        d = pd.read_csv(path, comment="#")
        return d.time_s.values, d.loadcell_V.values
    d = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";")
    return d.t.values, d.V.values


def block_uncertainty(x, n_per_block):
    """Standard error of the mean from non-overlapping block means."""
    n_blocks = len(x) // n_per_block
    means = x[: n_blocks * n_per_block].reshape(n_blocks, n_per_block).mean(axis=1)
    return means.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(n_blocks)


def dominant_frequency(x):
    """Frequency (Hz) of the largest peak in the force spectrum above 1 Hz."""
    f, pxx = signal.welch(x - x.mean(), fs=FS, nperseg=512)
    mask = f > 1.0
    return f[mask][np.argmax(pxx[mask])]


log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv")
sens = {path: fit_calibration(path) for _, path in CALIBRATIONS}
for path, (s, s_err) in sens.items():
    print(f"{path}: sensitivity {s:.5f} +/- {s_err:.5f} V/N")

rows = []
for r in log.itertuples():
    cal_path = calibration_for(r.date)
    s, s_err = sens[cal_path]
    t, v = read_run(os.path.join(RAW, r.date, f"run_{r.run_id:03d}.csv"))
    tare = v[(t >= TARE_WINDOW[0]) & (t < TARE_WINDOW[1])].mean()
    post = v[t > t[-1] - POST_WINDOW].mean()
    F = (v - tare) / s
    Fs = F[(t > STEADY_WINDOW[0]) & (t < STEADY_WINDOW[1])]
    zero_drift = (post - tare) / s
    rows.append({
        "run": r.run_id,
        "calibration": os.path.basename(cal_path),
        "sens_V_per_N": s,
        "sens_std_err": s_err,
        "F_mean": Fs.mean(),
        "F_std": Fs.std(ddof=1),
        "F_mean_unc": block_uncertainty(Fs, int(BLOCK_S * FS)),
        "f_peak_Hz": dominant_frequency(Fs),
        "zero_drift_N": zero_drift,
        "excluded": abs(zero_drift) > MAX_ZERO_DRIFT_N,
    })

out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
os.makedirs("processed", exist_ok=True)
out.to_csv("processed/forces.csv", index=False)
print(f"processed {len(out)} runs, excluded: {out.run[out.excluded].tolist()}")

# process tow tank runs -> mean drag force for each run
import glob
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA = "/Users/mkim/Dropbox/towtank/data/raw"
BATCHES = ["2025-10-14", "2025-11-03"]

cal = pd.read_csv("data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv")

print("sensitivity", sens)

rows = []
for b in BATCHES:
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(DATA, b, "run_*.csv"))):
        d = pd.read_csv(f, comment="#")
        tare = d.loadcell_V[d.time_s < 1.0].mean()
        F = (d.loadcell_V - tare) / sens
        steady = (d.time_s > 3) & (d.time_s < 8)
        rows.append({
            "run": int(os.path.basename(f)[4:7]),
            "F_mean": F[steady].mean(),
            "F_std": F[steady].std(),
        })

out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out.to_csv("processed/forces.csv", index=False)
print("done", len(out))

# process tow tank runs -> mean drag force for each run
#
# Handles both DAQ file formats (v2.1 comma-separated with "#" header, and the
# March 2026 semicolon format), picks the load cell calibration in effect on
# the run date, and flags runs whose zero drifted during the tow.
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import signal

RAW = "data/raw"
FS = 200.0  # Hz
TARE_WINDOW = (0.0, 1.0)  # s, carriage at rest before the tow
STEADY_WINDOW = (3.0, 8.0)  # s, constant-speed part of the tow
POST_WINDOW = 1.0  # s, last part of the record, carriage at rest again
BLOCK_S = 0.5  # s, block length for the random uncertainty of the mean
MAX_ZERO_DRIFT_N = 0.05  # N, |post-run zero - pre-run tare| above this -> excluded

# Calibration in effect from each date (load cell remounted 2026-03-10)
CALIBRATIONS = [
    ("2025-09-30", "data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv"),
    ("2026-03-10", "data/calibration/loadcell_2026-03.csv"),
]


def fit_calibration(path):
    """Linear fit of voltage vs applied force; returns slope (V/N) and its std error."""
    cal = pd.read_csv(path)
    force = cal.mass_g / 1000 * 9.81
    p, cov = np.polyfit(force, cal.voltage_V, 1, cov=True)
    return p[0], np.sqrt(cov[0, 0])


def calibration_for(date):
    valid = [c for c in CALIBRATIONS if c[0] <= date]
    return valid[-1][1]


def read_run(path):
    """Return time (s) and load cell voltage (V) for either DAQ file format."""
    with open(path) as f:
        first = f.readline()
    if first.startswith("#"):
        d = pd.read_csv(path, comment="#")
        return d.time_s.values, d.loadcell_V.values
    d = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";")
    return d.t.values, d.V.values


def block_uncertainty(x, n_per_block):
    """Standard error of the mean from non-overlapping block means."""
    n_blocks = len(x) // n_per_block
    means = x[: n_blocks * n_per_block].reshape(n_blocks, n_per_block).mean(axis=1)
    return means.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(n_blocks)


def dominant_frequency(x):
    """Frequency (Hz) of the largest peak in the force spectrum above 1 Hz."""
    f, pxx = signal.welch(x - x.mean(), fs=FS, nperseg=512)
    mask = f > 1.0
    return f[mask][np.argmax(pxx[mask])]


log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv")
sens = {path: fit_calibration(path) for _, path in CALIBRATIONS}
for path, (s, s_err) in sens.items():
    print(f"{path}: sensitivity {s:.5f} +/- {s_err:.5f} V/N")

rows = []
for r in log.itertuples():
    cal_path = calibration_for(r.date)
    s, s_err = sens[cal_path]
    t, v = read_run(os.path.join(RAW, r.date, f"run_{r.run_id:03d}.csv"))
    tare = v[(t >= TARE_WINDOW[0]) & (t < TARE_WINDOW[1])].mean()
    post = v[t > t[-1] - POST_WINDOW].mean()
    F = (v - tare) / s
    Fs = F[(t > STEADY_WINDOW[0]) & (t < STEADY_WINDOW[1])]
    zero_drift = (post - tare) / s
    rows.append({
        "run": r.run_id,
        "calibration": os.path.basename(cal_path),
        "sens_V_per_N": s,
        "sens_std_err": s_err,
        "F_mean": Fs.mean(),
        "F_std": Fs.std(ddof=1),
        "F_mean_unc": block_uncertainty(Fs, int(BLOCK_S * FS)),
        "f_peak_Hz": dominant_frequency(Fs),
        "zero_drift_N": zero_drift,
        "excluded": abs(zero_drift) > MAX_ZERO_DRIFT_N,
    })

out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
os.makedirs("processed", exist_ok=True)
out.to_csv("processed/forces.csv", index=False)
print(f"processed {len(out)} runs, excluded: {out.run[out.excluded].tolist()}")

# mean forces + run log -> Cd, Re, St per run, summary numbers, and the
# Cd/St vs Re figure and LaTeX table/macros used in the paper
import os

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

L = 0.60  # m, submerged length
TANK_W = 0.90  # m
TANK_H = 0.75  # m, water depth
G = 9.81
MASKELL_M = 2.5  # empirical blockage factor for the Maskell-type correction

# Fixed cylinder -> color/marker, ordered by diameter (validated palette)
STYLE = {
    "1in": ("#2a78d6", "o"),
    "1.5in": ("#eb6834", "s"),
    "2in": ("#1baf7a", "^"),
}
LABEL = {"1in": "$D$ = 25.4 mm", "1.5in": "$D$ = 38.1 mm", "2in": "$D$ = 50.8 mm"}


def water_density(T):
    """kg/m^3, Tanaka et al. (2001), T in deg C."""
    a1, a2, a3, a4, a5 = -3.983035, 301.797, 522528.9, 69.34881, 999.974950
    return a5 * (1 - (T + a1) ** 2 * (T + a2) / (a3 * (T + a4)))


def water_viscosity(T):
    """Pa s, Vogel-type correlation, T in deg C."""
    return 2.414e-5 * 10 ** (247.8 / (T + 273.15 - 140.0))


f = pd.read_csv("processed/forces.csv")
log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv")
df = f.merge(log, left_on="run", right_on="run_id")

D = df.diameter_mm / 1000
U = df.speed_m_s
df["rho"] = water_density(df.water_temp_c)
df["nu"] = water_viscosity(df.water_temp_c) / df.rho
df["Re"] = U * D / df.nu
df["Re_20C"] = U * D / 1.004e-6  # as in the original notebook, for comparison
q_A = 0.5 * df.rho * U**2 * D * L
df["Cd"] = df.F_mean / q_A
# random (block-averaged) + calibration slope uncertainty, added in quadrature
df["Cd_unc"] = df.Cd * np.sqrt(
    (df.F_mean_unc / df.F_mean) ** 2 + (df.sens_std_err / df.sens_V_per_N) ** 2
)
# drag fluctuates at twice the shedding frequency
df["St"] = df.f_peak_Hz / 2 * D / U
df["Fr"] = U / np.sqrt(G * D)
df["LD"] = L / D
df["blockage"] = D * L / (TANK_W * TANK_H)
df["Cd_corr"] = df.Cd / (1 + MASKELL_M * df.Cd * df.blockage)

os.makedirs("results", exist_ok=True)
cols = ["run", "cylinder", "diameter_mm", "speed_m_s", "water_temp_c", "rho", "nu",
        "Re", "Fr", "F_mean", "F_mean_unc", "Cd", "Cd_unc", "Cd_corr", "St",
        "zero_drift_N", "excluded"]
df[cols].to_csv("results/cd.csv", index=False)

good = df[~df.excluded]
order = ["1in", "1.5in", "2in"]
summary = good.groupby("cylinder").agg(
    D=("diameter_mm", "first"), n=("run", "size"), Cd=("Cd", "mean"),
    Cd_sd=("Cd", "std"), Cd_corr=("Cd_corr", "mean"), St=("St", "mean"),
    blockage=("blockage", "first"), LD=("LD", "first"),
    Re_min=("Re", "min"), Re_max=("Re", "max"),
).loc[order]
summary.to_csv("results/summary.csv")
print(summary.round(4).to_string())

# Pooled linear trend of Cd with log10(Re)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(np.log10(good.Re), good.Cd, 1)
re_shift = (df.Re_20C / df.Re - 1).agg(["min", "max"]) * 100
print(f"Cd trend: {slope:.3f} per decade of Re; Re(20C) overestimate "
      f"{re_shift['min']:.1f}-{re_shift['max']:.1f}%")

# --- Figure: Cd and St vs Re ---
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 9, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False})
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(4.5, 5.0), sharex=True,
                         gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})
ax_cd, ax_st = axes
for cyl in order:
    g = good[good.cylinder == cyl]
    color, marker = STYLE[cyl]
    kw = dict(color=color, marker=marker, ms=5, mec="white", mew=0.8, ls="none")
    ax_cd.errorbar(g.Re, g.Cd, yerr=g.Cd_unc, ecolor=color, elinewidth=1,
                   capsize=0, label=LABEL[cyl], **kw)
    ax_st.plot(g.Re, g.St, **kw)
bad = df[df.excluded]
ax_cd.plot(bad.Re, bad.Cd, marker="^", ms=5, mfc="none", mec="0.5", ls="none",
           label="Excluded (zero drift)")
for r in bad.itertuples():
    ax_cd.annotate(f"run {r.run}", (r.Re, r.Cd), xytext=(6, 0),
                   textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=8, color="0.35")
ax_cd.set_ylabel("$C_D$")
ax_cd.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
ax_st.set_ylabel("St")
ax_st.set_ylim(0.15, 0.25)
ax_st.set_xscale("log")
ax_st.set_xlabel("Re")
for ax, tag in zip(axes, "ab"):
    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="0.9", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.text(0.02, 0.95, f"({tag})", transform=ax.transAxes, va="top")
fig.tight_layout()
os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.pdf")
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.png", dpi=200)

# --- LaTeX outputs for the paper ---
os.makedirs("paper/generated", exist_ok=True)


def fmt_sci(x):
    e = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
    return rf"{x / 10**e:.1f}\times10^{{{e}}}"


name = {"1in": "A", "1.5in": "B", "2in": "C"}
macros = {
    "NRuns": len(df),
    "NGood": len(good),
    "ReMin": fmt_sci(good.Re.min()),
    "ReMax": fmt_sci(good.Re.max()),
    "TMin": f"{df.water_temp_c.min():.1f}",
    "TMax": f"{df.water_temp_c.max():.1f}",
    "CdMean": f"{good.Cd.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSD": f"{good.Cd.std():.2f}",
    "CdCorrMean": f"{good.Cd_corr.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSlope": f"{slope:.3f}",
    "StMean": f"{good.St.mean():.3f}",
    "StSD": f"{good.St.std():.3f}",
    "CdUncMax": f"{(good.Cd_unc / good.Cd).max() * 100:.1f}",
    "ReShiftMin": f"{re_shift['min']:.0f}",
    "ReShiftMax": f"{re_shift['max']:.0f}",
    "FrMax": f"{good.Fr.max():.1f}",
    "FrMin": f"{good.Fr.min():.2f}",
    "ExclRun": ", ".join(str(r) for r in bad.run),
    "ExclDrift": f"{bad.zero_drift_N.abs().max():.1f}",
    "ExclCd": f"{bad.Cd.max():.2f}",
    "GoodDriftMax": f"{good.zero_drift_N.abs().max() * 1000:.0f}",
    "SensA": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date < '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
    "SensB": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date >= '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
}
for cyl, s in summary.iterrows():
    n = name[cyl]
    macros[f"Cd{n}"] = f"{s.Cd:.2f}"
    macros[f"CdSD{n}"] = f"{s.Cd_sd:.2f}"
    macros[f"CdCorr{n}"] = f"{s.Cd_corr:.2f}"
    macros[f"Blockage{n}"] = f"{s.blockage * 100:.1f}"
    macros[f"LD{n}"] = f"{s.LD:.1f}"
with open("paper/generated/macros.tex", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("% generated by analyze.py -- do not edit\n")
    for k, v in macros.items():
        fh.write(f"\\newcommand{{\\{k}}}{{{v}}}\n")

lines = [
    "% generated by analyze.py -- do not edit",
    r"\begin{tabular}{ccccccc}",
    r"\toprule",
    r"$D$ (mm) & $L/D$ & $S/C$ (\%) & $N$ & Re range & $\overline{C_D}$ "
    r"& $\overline{C_D}_{,c}$ \\",
    r"\midrule",
]
for cyl, s in summary.iterrows():
    lines.append(
        rf"{s.D:.1f} & {s.LD:.1f} & {s.blockage * 100:.1f} & {s.n} & "
        rf"${fmt_sci(s.Re_min)}$--${fmt_sci(s.Re_max)}$ & "
        rf"{s.Cd:.2f} $\pm$ {s.Cd_sd:.2f} & {s.Cd_corr:.2f} \\"
    )
lines += [r"\bottomrule", r"\end{tabular}", ""]
with open("paper/generated/summary_table.tex", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines))

# mean forces + run log -> Cd, Re, St per run, summary numbers, and the
# Cd/St vs Re figure and LaTeX table/macros used in the paper
import os

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

L = 0.60  # m, submerged length
TANK_W = 0.90  # m
TANK_H = 0.75  # m, water depth
G = 9.81
MASKELL_M = 2.5  # empirical blockage factor for the Maskell-type correction

# Fixed cylinder -> color/marker, ordered by diameter (validated palette)
STYLE = {
    "1in": ("#2a78d6", "o"),
    "1.5in": ("#eb6834", "s"),
    "2in": ("#1baf7a", "^"),
}
LABEL = {"1in": "$D$ = 25.4 mm", "1.5in": "$D$ = 38.1 mm", "2in": "$D$ = 50.8 mm"}


def water_density(T):
    """kg/m^3, Tanaka et al. (2001), T in deg C."""
    a1, a2, a3, a4, a5 = -3.983035, 301.797, 522528.9, 69.34881, 999.974950
    return a5 * (1 - (T + a1) ** 2 * (T + a2) / (a3 * (T + a4)))


def water_viscosity(T):
    """Pa s, Vogel-type correlation, T in deg C."""
    return 2.414e-5 * 10 ** (247.8 / (T + 273.15 - 140.0))


f = pd.read_csv("processed/forces.csv")
log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv")
df = f.merge(log, left_on="run", right_on="run_id")

D = df.diameter_mm / 1000
U = df.speed_m_s
df["rho"] = water_density(df.water_temp_c)
df["nu"] = water_viscosity(df.water_temp_c) / df.rho
df["Re"] = U * D / df.nu
df["Re_20C"] = U * D / 1.004e-6  # as in the original notebook, for comparison
q_A = 0.5 * df.rho * U**2 * D * L
df["Cd"] = df.F_mean / q_A
# random (block-averaged) + calibration slope uncertainty, added in quadrature
df["Cd_unc"] = df.Cd * np.sqrt(
    (df.F_mean_unc / df.F_mean) ** 2 + (df.sens_std_err / df.sens_V_per_N) ** 2
)
# drag fluctuates at twice the shedding frequency
df["St"] = df.f_peak_Hz / 2 * D / U
df["Fr"] = U / np.sqrt(G * D)
df["LD"] = L / D
df["blockage"] = D * L / (TANK_W * TANK_H)
df["Cd_corr"] = df.Cd / (1 + MASKELL_M * df.Cd * df.blockage)

os.makedirs("results", exist_ok=True)
cols = ["run", "cylinder", "diameter_mm", "speed_m_s", "water_temp_c", "rho", "nu",
        "Re", "Fr", "F_mean", "F_mean_unc", "Cd", "Cd_unc", "Cd_corr", "St",
        "zero_drift_N", "excluded"]
df[cols].to_csv("results/cd.csv", index=False)

good = df[~df.excluded]
order = ["1in", "1.5in", "2in"]
summary = good.groupby("cylinder").agg(
    D=("diameter_mm", "first"), n=("run", "size"), Cd=("Cd", "mean"),
    Cd_sd=("Cd", "std"), Cd_corr=("Cd_corr", "mean"), St=("St", "mean"),
    blockage=("blockage", "first"), LD=("LD", "first"),
    Re_min=("Re", "min"), Re_max=("Re", "max"),
).loc[order]
summary.to_csv("results/summary.csv")
print(summary.round(4).to_string())

# Pooled linear trend of Cd with log10(Re)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(np.log10(good.Re), good.Cd, 1)
re_shift = (df.Re_20C / df.Re - 1).agg(["min", "max"]) * 100
print(f"Cd trend: {slope:.3f} per decade of Re; Re(20C) overestimate "
      f"{re_shift['min']:.1f}-{re_shift['max']:.1f}%")

# --- Figure: Cd and St vs Re ---
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 9, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False})
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(4.5, 5.0), sharex=True,
                         gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})
ax_cd, ax_st = axes
for cyl in order:
    g = good[good.cylinder == cyl]
    color, marker = STYLE[cyl]
    kw = dict(color=color, marker=marker, ms=5, mec="white", mew=0.8, ls="none")
    ax_cd.errorbar(g.Re, g.Cd, yerr=g.Cd_unc, ecolor=color, elinewidth=1,
                   capsize=0, label=LABEL[cyl], **kw)
    ax_st.plot(g.Re, g.St, **kw)
bad = df[df.excluded]
ax_cd.plot(bad.Re, bad.Cd, marker="^", ms=5, mfc="none", mec="0.5", ls="none",
           label="Excluded (zero drift)")
for r in bad.itertuples():
    ax_cd.annotate(f"run {r.run}", (r.Re, r.Cd), xytext=(6, 0),
                   textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=8, color="0.35")
ax_cd.set_ylabel("$C_D$")
ax_cd.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
ax_st.set_ylabel("St")
ax_st.set_ylim(0.15, 0.25)
ax_st.set_xscale("log")
ax_st.set_xlabel("Re")
for ax, tag in zip(axes, "ab"):
    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="0.9", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.text(0.02, 0.95, f"({tag})", transform=ax.transAxes, va="top")
fig.tight_layout()
os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.pdf")
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.png", dpi=200)

# --- LaTeX outputs for the paper ---
os.makedirs("paper/generated", exist_ok=True)


def fmt_sci(x):
    e = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
    return rf"{x / 10**e:.1f}\times10^{{{e}}}"


name = {"1in": "A", "1.5in": "B", "2in": "C"}
macros = {
    "NRuns": len(df),
    "NGood": len(good),
    "ReMin": fmt_sci(good.Re.min()),
    "ReMax": fmt_sci(good.Re.max()),
    "TMin": f"{df.water_temp_c.min():.1f}",
    "TMax": f"{df.water_temp_c.max():.1f}",
    "CdMean": f"{good.Cd.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSD": f"{good.Cd.std():.2f}",
    "CdCorrMean": f"{good.Cd_corr.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSlope": f"{slope:.3f}",
    "StMean": f"{good.St.mean():.3f}",
    "StSD": f"{good.St.std():.3f}",
    "CdUncMax": f"{(good.Cd_unc / good.Cd).max() * 100:.1f}",
    "ReShiftMin": f"{re_shift['min']:.0f}",
    "ReShiftMax": f"{re_shift['max']:.0f}",
    "FrMax": f"{good.Fr.max():.1f}",
    "FrMin": f"{good.Fr.min():.2f}",
    "ExclRun": ", ".join(str(r) for r in bad.run),
    "ExclDrift": f"{bad.zero_drift_N.abs().max():.1f}",
    "ExclCd": f"{bad.Cd.max():.2f}",
    "GoodDriftMax": f"{good.zero_drift_N.abs().max() * 1000:.0f}",
    "SensA": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date < '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
    "SensB": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date >= '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
}
for cyl, s in summary.iterrows():
    n = name[cyl]
    macros[f"Cd{n}"] = f"{s.Cd:.2f}"
    macros[f"CdSD{n}"] = f"{s.Cd_sd:.2f}"
    macros[f"CdCorr{n}"] = f"{s.Cd_corr:.2f}"
    macros[f"Blockage{n}"] = f"{s.blockage * 100:.1f}"
    macros[f"LD{n}"] = f"{s.LD:.1f}"
with open("paper/generated/macros.tex", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("% generated by analyze.py -- do not edit\n")
    for k, v in macros.items():
        fh.write(f"\\newcommand{{\\{k}}}{{{v}}}\n")

lines = [
    "% generated by analyze.py -- do not edit",
    r"\begin{tabular}{ccccccc}",
    r"\toprule",
    r"$D$ (mm) & $L/D$ & $S/C$ (\%) & $N$ & Re range & $\overline{C_D}$ "
    r"& $\overline{C_D}_{,c}$ \\",
    r"\midrule",
]
for cyl, s in summary.iterrows():
    lines.append(
        rf"{s.D:.1f} & {s.LD:.1f} & {s.blockage * 100:.1f} & {s.n} & "
        rf"${fmt_sci(s.Re_min)}$--${fmt_sci(s.Re_max)}$ & "
        rf"{s.Cd:.2f} $\pm$ {s.Cd_sd:.2f} & {s.Cd_corr:.2f} \\"
    )
lines += [r"\bottomrule", r"\end{tabular}", ""]
with open("paper/generated/summary_table.tex", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines))

    (df.F_mean_unc / df.F_mean) ** 2 + (df.sens_std_err / df.sens_V_per_N) ** 2
)
# drag fluctuates at twice the shedding frequency
df["St"] = df.f_peak_Hz / 2 * D / U
df["Fr"] = U / np.sqrt(G * D)
df["LD"] = L / D
df["blockage"] = D * L / (TANK_W * TANK_H)
df["Cd_corr"] = df.Cd / (1 + MASKELL_M * df.Cd * df.blockage)

os.makedirs("results", exist_ok=True)
cols = ["run", "cylinder", "diameter_mm", "speed_m_s", "water_temp_c", "rho", "nu",
        "Re", "Fr", "F_mean", "F_mean_unc", "Cd", "Cd_unc", "Cd_corr", "St",
        "zero_drift_N", "excluded"]
df[cols].to_csv("results/cd.csv", index=False)

good = df[~df.excluded]
order = ["1in", "1.5in", "2in"]
summary = good.groupby("cylinder").agg(
    D=("diameter_mm", "first"), n=("run", "size"), Cd=("Cd", "mean"),
    Cd_sd=("Cd", "std"), Cd_corr=("Cd_corr", "mean"), St=("St", "mean"),
    blockage=("blockage", "first"), LD=("LD", "first"),
    Re_min=("Re", "min"), Re_max=("Re", "max"),
).loc[order]
summary.to_csv("results/summary.csv")
print(summary.round(4).to_string())

# Pooled linear trend of Cd with log10(Re)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(np.log10(good.Re), good.Cd, 1)
re_shift = (df.Re_20C / df.Re - 1).agg(["min", "max"]) * 100
print(f"Cd trend: {slope:.3f} per decade of Re; Re(20C) overestimate "
      f"{re_shift['min']:.1f}-{re_shift['max']:.1f}%")

# --- Figure: Cd and St vs Re ---
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 9, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False})
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(4.5, 5.0), sharex=True,
                         gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})
ax_cd, ax_st = axes
for cyl in order:
    g = good[good.cylinder == cyl]
    color, marker = STYLE[cyl]
    kw = dict(color=color, marker=marker, ms=5, mec="white", mew=0.8, ls="none")
    ax_cd.errorbar(g.Re, g.Cd, yerr=g.Cd_unc, ecolor=color, elinewidth=1,
                   capsize=0, label=LABEL[cyl], **kw)
    ax_st.plot(g.Re, g.St, **kw)
bad = df[df.excluded]
ax_cd.plot(bad.Re, bad.Cd, marker="^", ms=5, mfc="none", mec="0.5", ls="none",
           label="Excluded (zero drift)")
for r in bad.itertuples():
    ax_cd.annotate(f"run {r.run}", (r.Re, r.Cd), xytext=(6, 0),
                   textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=8, color="0.35")
ax_cd.set_ylabel("$C_D$")
handles, labels = ax_cd.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax_cd.legend(handles[1:] + handles[:1], labels[1:] + labels[:1], frameon=False,
             fontsize=8, ncol=2, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0))
ax_st.set_ylabel("St")
ax_st.set_ylim(0.15, 0.25)
ax_st.set_xscale("log")
ax_st.set_xlabel("Re")
ax_st.set_xticks([5e3, 1e4, 2e4, 5e4], ["5000", "10 000", "20 000", "50 000"])
ax_st.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(plt.NullFormatter())
for ax, tag in zip(axes, "ab"):
    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="0.9", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.text(0.02, 0.95, f"({tag})", transform=ax.transAxes, va="top")
fig.tight_layout()
os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.pdf")
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.png", dpi=200)

# --- LaTeX outputs for the paper ---
os.makedirs("paper/generated", exist_ok=True)


def fmt_sci(x):
    e = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
    return rf"{x / 10**e:.1f}\times10^{{{e}}}"


name = {"1in": "A", "1.5in": "B", "2in": "C"}
macros = {
    "NRuns": len(df),
    "NGood": len(good),
    "ReMin": fmt_sci(good.Re.min()),
    "ReMax": fmt_sci(good.Re.max()),
    "TMin": f"{df.water_temp_c.min():.1f}",
    "TMax": f"{df.water_temp_c.max():.1f}",
    "CdMean": f"{good.Cd.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSD": f"{good.Cd.std():.2f}",
    "CdCorrMean": f"{good.Cd_corr.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSlope": f"{slope:.3f}",
    "StMean": f"{good.St.mean():.3f}",
    "StSD": f"{good.St.std():.3f}",
    "CdUncMax": f"{(good.Cd_unc / good.Cd).max() * 100:.1f}",
    "ReShiftMin": f"{re_shift['min']:.0f}",
    "ReShiftMax": f"{re_shift['max']:.0f}",
    "FrMax": f"{good.Fr.max():.1f}",
    "FrMin": f"{good.Fr.min():.2f}",
    "ExclRun": ", ".join(str(r) for r in bad.run),
    "ExclDrift": f"{bad.zero_drift_N.abs().max():.1f}",
    "ExclCd": f"{bad.Cd.max():.2f}",
    "GoodDriftMax": f"{good.zero_drift_N.abs().max() * 1000:.0f}",
    "SensA": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date < '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
    "SensB": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date >= '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
}
for cyl, s in summary.iterrows():
    n = name[cyl]
    macros[f"Cd{n}"] = f"{s.Cd:.2f}"
    macros[f"CdSD{n}"] = f"{s.Cd_sd:.2f}"
    macros[f"CdCorr{n}"] = f"{s.Cd_corr:.2f}"
    macros[f"Blockage{n}"] = f"{s.blockage * 100:.1f}"
    macros[f"LD{n}"] = f"{s.LD:.1f}"
with open("paper/generated/macros.tex", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("% generated by analyze.py -- do not edit\n")
    for k, v in macros.items():
        fh.write(f"\\newcommand{{\\{k}}}{{{v}}}\n")

lines = [
    "% generated by analyze.py -- do not edit",
    r"\begin{tabular}{ccccccc}",
    r"\toprule",
    r"$D$ (mm) & $L/D$ & $S/C$ (\%) & $N$ & Re range & $\overline{C_D}$ "
    r"& $\overline{C_D}_{,c}$ \\",
    r"\midrule",
]
for cyl, s in summary.iterrows():
    lines.append(
        rf"{s.D:.1f} & {s.LD:.1f} & {s.blockage * 100:.1f} & {s.n} & "
        rf"${fmt_sci(s.Re_min)}$--${fmt_sci(s.Re_max)}$ & "
        rf"{s.Cd:.2f} $\pm$ {s.Cd_sd:.2f} & {s.Cd_corr:.2f} \\"
    )
lines += [r"\bottomrule", r"\end{tabular}", ""]
with open("paper/generated/summary_table.tex", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

forces = pd.read_csv("processed/forces.csv").set_index("run")

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://docs.calkit.org/schemas/calkit.json
environments:
  py:
    path: requirements.txt
    kind: uv-venv
    python: '3.12'
    description: Python env for processing and plotting
pipeline:
  stages:
    process:
      kind: python-script
      environment: py
      inputs:
        - data/raw
        - data/calibration
        - data/run_log.csv
      outputs:
        - path: processed/forces.csv
          storage: git
      script_path: process.py
    analyze:
      kind: python-script
      environment: py
      inputs:
        - processed/forces.csv
        - data/run_log.csv
      outputs:
        - path: results/cd.csv
          storage: git
        - path: results/summary.csv
          storage: git
        - path: figures/cd_st_vs_re.pdf
          storage: git
        - path: figures/cd_st_vs_re.png
          storage: git
        - path: paper/generated/macros.tex
          storage: git
        - path: paper/generated/summary_table.tex
          storage: git
      script_path: analyze.py
    plot-timeseries:
      kind: python-script
      environment: py
      inputs:
        - processed/forces.csv
        - data/raw/2025-10-14/run_005.csv
      outputs:

# the run date, and flags runs whose zero drifted during the tow.
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import signal

RAW = "data/raw"
FS = 200.0  # Hz
TARE_WINDOW = (0.0, 1.0)  # s, carriage at rest before the tow
STEADY_WINDOW = (3.0, 8.0)  # s, constant-speed part of the tow
POST_WINDOW = 1.0  # s, last part of the record, carriage at rest again
BLOCK_S = 0.5  # s, block length for the random uncertainty of the mean
MAX_ZERO_DRIFT_N = 0.05  # N, |post-run zero - pre-run tare| above this -> excluded

# Calibration in effect from each date (load cell remounted 2026-03-10)
CALIBRATIONS = [
    ("2025-09-30", "data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv"),
    ("2026-03-10", "data/calibration/loadcell_2026-03.csv"),
]


def fit_calibration(path):
    """Linear fit of voltage vs applied force; returns slope (V/N) and its std error."""
    cal = pd.read_csv(path)
    force = cal.mass_g / 1000 * 9.81
    p, cov = np.polyfit(force, cal.voltage_V, 1, cov=True)
    return p[0], np.sqrt(cov[0, 0])


def calibration_for(date):
    valid = [c for c in CALIBRATIONS if c[0] <= date]
    return valid[-1][1]


def read_run(path):
    """Return time (s) and load cell voltage (V) for either DAQ file format."""
    with open(path) as f:
        first = f.readline()
    if first.startswith("#"):
        d = pd.read_csv(path, comment="#")
        return d.time_s.values, d.loadcell_V.values
    d = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";")
    return d.t.values, d.V.values


def block_uncertainty(x, n_per_block):
    """Standard error of the mean from non-overlapping block means."""
    n_blocks = len(x) // n_per_block
    means = x[: n_blocks * n_per_block].reshape(n_blocks, n_per_block).mean(axis=1)
    return means.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(n_blocks)


def dominant_frequency(x):
    """Frequency (Hz) of the largest peak in the force spectrum above 1 Hz."""
    # Whole steady window with zero padding: the window is only ~5 s long
    f, pxx = signal.periodogram(x - x.mean(), fs=FS, window="hann", nfft=2**15)
    mask = f > 1.0
    return f[mask][np.argmax(pxx[mask])]


log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv")
sens = {path: fit_calibration(path) for _, path in CALIBRATIONS}
for path, (s, s_err) in sens.items():
    print(f"{path}: sensitivity {s:.5f} +/- {s_err:.5f} V/N")

rows = []
for r in log.itertuples():
    cal_path = calibration_for(r.date)
    s, s_err = sens[cal_path]
    t, v = read_run(os.path.join(RAW, r.date, f"run_{r.run_id:03d}.csv"))

        "sens_std_err": s_err,

        "f_peak_Hz": dominant_frequency(Fs),
        "zero_drift_N": zero_drift,
        "excluded": abs(zero_drift) > MAX_ZERO_DRIFT_N,
    })

out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
os.makedirs("processed", exist_ok=True)
out.to_csv("processed/forces.csv", index=False)
print(f"processed {len(out)} runs, excluded: {out.run[out.excluded].tolist()}")

environments:

  stages:
    process:

      environment: py
      inputs:
        - data/raw
        - data/calibration
        - data/run_log.csv
      outputs:
        - path: processed/forces.csv
          storage: git
      script_path: process.py
    analyze:
      kind: python-script
      environment: py
      inputs:
        - processed/forces.csv
        - data/run_log.csv
      outputs:
        - path: results/cd.csv
          storage: git
        - path: results/summary.csv
          storage: git
        - path: figures/cd_st_vs_re.pdf
          storage: git
        - path: figures/cd_st_vs_re.png
          storage: git
        - path: paper/generated/macros.tex
          storage: git
        - path: paper/generated/summary_table.tex
          storage: git
      script_path: analyze.py
    plot-timeseries:
      kind: python-script
      environment: py
      inputs:
        - processed/forces.csv

        - path: figures/timeseries_run005.pdf
          storage: git

# mean forces + run log -> Cd, Re, St per run, summary numbers, and the
# Cd/St vs Re figure and LaTeX table/macros used in the paper
import os

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

L = 0.60  # m, submerged length
TANK_W = 0.90  # m
TANK_H = 0.75  # m, water depth
G = 9.81
MASKELL_M = 2.5  # empirical blockage factor for the Maskell-type correction

# Fixed cylinder -> color/marker, ordered by diameter (validated palette)
STYLE = {
    "1in": ("#2a78d6", "o"),
    "1.5in": ("#eb6834", "s"),
    "2in": ("#1baf7a", "^"),
}
LABEL = {"1in": "$D$ = 25.4 mm", "1.5in": "$D$ = 38.1 mm", "2in": "$D$ = 50.8 mm"}


def water_density(T):
    """kg/m^3, Tanaka et al. (2001), T in deg C."""
    a1, a2, a3, a4, a5 = -3.983035, 301.797, 522528.9, 69.34881, 999.974950
    return a5 * (1 - (T + a1) ** 2 * (T + a2) / (a3 * (T + a4)))


def water_viscosity(T):
    """Pa s, Vogel-type correlation, T in deg C."""
    return 2.414e-5 * 10 ** (247.8 / (T + 273.15 - 140.0))


f = pd.read_csv("processed/forces.csv")
log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv")
df = f.merge(log, left_on="run", right_on="run_id")

D = df.diameter_mm / 1000
U = df.speed_m_s
df["rho"] = water_density(df.water_temp_c)
df["nu"] = water_viscosity(df.water_temp_c) / df.rho
df["Re"] = U * D / df.nu
df["Re_20C"] = U * D / 1.004e-6  # as in the original notebook, for comparison
q_A = 0.5 * df.rho * U**2 * D * L
df["Cd"] = df.F_mean / q_A
# random (block-averaged) + calibration slope uncertainty, added in quadrature
df["Cd_unc"] = df.Cd * np.sqrt(
    (df.F_mean_unc / df.F_mean) ** 2 + (df.sens_std_err / df.sens_V_per_N) ** 2
)
# drag fluctuates at twice the shedding frequency
df["St"] = df.f_peak_Hz / 2 * D / U
df["Fr"] = U / np.sqrt(G * D)
df["LD"] = L / D
df["blockage"] = D * L / (TANK_W * TANK_H)
df["Cd_corr"] = df.Cd / (1 + MASKELL_M * df.Cd * df.blockage)

os.makedirs("results", exist_ok=True)
cols = ["run", "cylinder", "diameter_mm", "speed_m_s", "water_temp_c", "rho", "nu",
        "Re", "Fr", "F_mean", "F_mean_unc", "Cd", "Cd_unc", "Cd_corr", "St",
        "zero_drift_N", "excluded"]
df[cols].to_csv("results/cd.csv", index=False)

good = df[~df.excluded]
order = ["1in", "1.5in", "2in"]
summary = good.groupby("cylinder").agg(
    D=("diameter_mm", "first"), n=("run", "size"), Cd=("Cd", "mean"),
    Cd_sd=("Cd", "std"), Cd_corr=("Cd_corr", "mean"), St=("St", "mean"),
    blockage=("blockage", "first"), LD=("LD", "first"),
    Re_min=("Re", "min"), Re_max=("Re", "max"),
).loc[order]
summary.to_csv("results/summary.csv")
print(summary.round(4).to_string())

# Pooled linear trend of Cd with log10(Re)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(np.log10(good.Re), good.Cd, 1)
re_shift = (df.Re_20C / df.Re - 1).agg(["min", "max"]) * 100
print(f"Cd trend: {slope:.3f} per decade of Re; Re(20C) overestimate "
      f"{re_shift['min']:.1f}-{re_shift['max']:.1f}%")

# --- Figure: Cd and St vs Re ---
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 9, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False})
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(4.5, 5.0), sharex=True,
                         gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})
ax_cd, ax_st = axes
for cyl in order:
    g = good[good.cylinder == cyl]
    color, marker = STYLE[cyl]
    kw = dict(color=color, marker=marker, ms=5, mec="white", mew=0.8, ls="none")
    ax_cd.errorbar(g.Re, g.Cd, yerr=g.Cd_unc, ecolor=color, elinewidth=1,
                   capsize=0, label=LABEL[cyl], **kw)
    ax_st.plot(g.Re, g.St, **kw)
bad = df[df.excluded]
ax_cd.plot(bad.Re, bad.Cd, marker="^", ms=5, mfc="none", mec="0.5", ls="none",
           label="Excluded (zero drift)")
for r in bad.itertuples():
    ax_cd.annotate(f"run {r.run}", (r.Re, r.Cd), xytext=(6, 0),
                   textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=8, color="0.35")
ax_cd.set_ylabel("$C_D$")
handles, labels = ax_cd.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax_cd.legend(handles[1:] + handles[:1], labels[1:] + labels[:1], frameon=False,
             fontsize=8, ncol=2, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0))
ax_st.set_ylabel("St")
ax_st.set_ylim(0.15, 0.25)
ax_st.set_xscale("log")
ax_st.set_xlabel("Re")
ax_st.set_xticks([5e3, 1e4, 2e4, 5e4], ["5000", "10 000", "20 000", "50 000"])
ax_st.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(plt.NullFormatter())
for ax, tag in zip(axes, "ab"):
    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="0.9", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.text(0.02, 0.95, f"({tag})", transform=ax.transAxes, va="top")

# mean forces + run log -> Cd, Re, St per run, summary numbers, and the
# Cd/St vs Re figure and LaTeX table/macros used in the paper
import os

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

L = 0.60  # m, submerged length
TANK_W = 0.90  # m
TANK_H = 0.75  # m, water depth
G = 9.81
MASKELL_M = 2.5  # empirical blockage factor for the Maskell-type correction

# Fixed cylinder -> color/marker, ordered by diameter (validated palette)
STYLE = {
    "1in": ("#2a78d6", "o"),
    "1.5in": ("#eb6834", "s"),
    "2in": ("#1baf7a", "^"),
}
LABEL = {"1in": "$D$ = 25.4 mm", "1.5in": "$D$ = 38.1 mm", "2in": "$D$ = 50.8 mm"}


def water_density(T):
    """kg/m^3, Tanaka et al. (2001), T in deg C."""
    a1, a2, a3, a4, a5 = -3.983035, 301.797, 522528.9, 69.34881, 999.974950
    return a5 * (1 - (T + a1) ** 2 * (T + a2) / (a3 * (T + a4)))


def water_viscosity(T):
    """Pa s, Vogel-type correlation, T in deg C."""
    return 2.414e-5 * 10 ** (247.8 / (T + 273.15 - 140.0))


f = pd.read_csv("processed/forces.csv")
log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv")
df = f.merge(log, left_on="run", right_on="run_id")

D = df.diameter_mm / 1000
U = df.speed_m_s
df["rho"] = water_density(df.water_temp_c)
df["nu"] = water_viscosity(df.water_temp_c) / df.rho
df["Re"] = U * D / df.nu
df["Re_20C"] = U * D / 1.004e-6  # as in the original notebook, for comparison
q_A = 0.5 * df.rho * U**2 * D * L
df["Cd"] = df.F_mean / q_A
# random (block-averaged) + calibration slope uncertainty, added in quadrature
df["Cd_unc"] = df.Cd * np.sqrt(
    (df.F_mean_unc / df.F_mean) ** 2 + (df.sens_std_err / df.sens_V_per_N) ** 2
)
# drag fluctuates at twice the shedding frequency
df["St"] = df.f_peak_Hz / 2 * D / U
df["Fr"] = U / np.sqrt(G * D)
df["LD"] = L / D
df["blockage"] = D * L / (TANK_W * TANK_H)
df["Cd_corr"] = df.Cd / (1 + MASKELL_M * df.Cd * df.blockage)

os.makedirs("results", exist_ok=True)
cols = ["run", "cylinder", "diameter_mm", "speed_m_s", "water_temp_c", "rho", "nu",
        "Re", "Fr", "F_mean", "F_mean_unc", "Cd", "Cd_unc", "Cd_corr", "St",
        "zero_drift_N", "excluded"]
df[cols].to_csv("results/cd.csv", index=False)

good = df[~df.excluded]
order = ["1in", "1.5in", "2in"]
summary = good.groupby("cylinder").agg(
    D=("diameter_mm", "first"), n=("run", "size"), Cd=("Cd", "mean"),
    Cd_sd=("Cd", "std"), Cd_corr=("Cd_corr", "mean"), St=("St", "mean"),
    blockage=("blockage", "first"), LD=("LD", "first"),
    Re_min=("Re", "min"), Re_max=("Re", "max"),
).loc[order]
summary.to_csv("results/summary.csv")
print(summary.round(4).to_string())

# Pooled linear trend of Cd with log10(Re)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(np.log10(good.Re), good.Cd, 1)
re_shift = (df.Re_20C / df.Re - 1).agg(["min", "max"]) * 100
print(f"Cd trend: {slope:.3f} per decade of Re; Re(20C) overestimate "
      f"{re_shift['min']:.1f}-{re_shift['max']:.1f}%")

# --- Figure: Cd and St vs Re ---
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 9, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False})
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(4.5, 5.0), sharex=True,
                         gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})
ax_cd, ax_st = axes
for cyl in order:
    g = good[good.cylinder == cyl]
    color, marker = STYLE[cyl]
    kw = dict(color=color, marker=marker, ms=5, mec="white", mew=0.8, ls="none")
    ax_cd.errorbar(g.Re, g.Cd, yerr=g.Cd_unc, ecolor=color, elinewidth=1,
                   capsize=0, label=LABEL[cyl], **kw)
    ax_st.plot(g.Re, g.St, **kw)
bad = df[df.excluded]
ax_cd.plot(bad.Re, bad.Cd, marker="^", ms=5, mfc="none", mec="0.5", ls="none",
           label="Excluded (zero drift)")
for r in bad.itertuples():
    ax_cd.annotate(f"run {r.run}", (r.Re, r.Cd), xytext=(6, 0),
                   textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=8, color="0.35")
ax_cd.set_ylabel("$C_D$")
handles, labels = ax_cd.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax_cd.legend(handles[1:] + handles[:1], labels[1:] + labels[:1], frameon=False,
             fontsize=8, ncol=2, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0))
ax_st.set_ylabel("St")
ax_st.set_ylim(0.15, 0.25)
ax_st.set_xscale("log")
ax_st.set_xlabel("Re")
ax_st.set_xticks([5e3, 1e4, 2e4, 5e4], ["5000", "10 000", "20 000", "50 000"])
ax_st.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(plt.NullFormatter())
for ax, tag in zip(axes, "ab"):
    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="0.9", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.text(0.02, 0.95, f"({tag})", transform=ax.transAxes, va="top")
fig.tight_layout()
os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.pdf")
fig.savefig("figures/cd_st_vs_re.png", dpi=200)

# --- LaTeX outputs for the paper ---
os.makedirs("paper/generated", exist_ok=True)


def fmt_sci(x):
    e = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
    return rf"{x / 10**e:.1f}\times10^{{{e}}}"


name = {"1in": "A", "1.5in": "B", "2in": "C"}
macros = {
    "NRuns": len(df),
    "NGood": len(good),
    "ReMin": fmt_sci(good.Re.min()),
    "ReMax": fmt_sci(good.Re.max()),
    "TMin": f"{df.water_temp_c.min():.1f}",
    "TMax": f"{df.water_temp_c.max():.1f}",
    "CdMean": f"{good.Cd.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSD": f"{good.Cd.std():.2f}",
    "CdCorrMean": f"{good.Cd_corr.mean():.2f}",
    "CdSlope": f"{slope:.3f}",
    "StMean": f"{good.St.mean():.3f}",
    "StDev": f"{(good.St - good.St.mean()).abs().max():.4f}",
    "CdUncMax": f"{(good.Cd_unc / good.Cd).max() * 100:.1f}",
    "CdUncMed": f"{(good.Cd_unc / good.Cd).median() * 100:.1f}",
    "ReShiftMin": f"{re_shift['min']:.0f}",
    "ReShiftMax": f"{re_shift['max']:.0f}",
    "FrMax": f"{good.Fr.max():.1f}",
    "FrMin": f"{good.Fr.min():.2f}",
    "ExclRun": ", ".join(str(r) for r in bad.run),
    "ExclDrift": f"{bad.zero_drift_N.abs().max():.1f}",
    "ExclCd": f"{bad.Cd.max():.2f}",
    "GoodDriftMax": f"{good.zero_drift_N.abs().max() * 1000:.0f}",
    "SensA": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date < '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
    "SensB": f"{df.sens_V_per_N[df.date >= '2026-03-10'].iloc[0] * 1000:.2f}",
}
for cyl, s in summary.iterrows():

`process_b3.py`, `processed/forces_b3.csv` and `analysis.ipynb` are the
earlier workflow, superseded by the pipeline above.
old_matlab/ is Jamie's original processing script, kept for reference.

content.text:
I've written a 6-page first draft at `paper/paper.pdf` (source: `paper/paper.tex`). It's built by a Calkit pipeline, so `calkit run` regenerates everything from your raw data to the PDF. Every number in the text, table and abstract is generated from the data, so the paper updates when the analysis changes. Anything I couldn't get from your files is marked with a red **[TODO]**.

**Things I found that change your results:**
- **Run 17 should be dropped.** You suspected its zero was off, and it is. After the run the load cell sits 4.2 N off zero, while every other run returns to within 3 mN. During the tow its signal keeps climbing instead of levelling off. The pipeline now excludes any run whose zero shifts by more than 0.05 N, which catches only run 17.
- **There's no diameter effect.** Your notebook had Cd = 1.18 for the 2in and 1.14 for the 1in, but run 17 was inflating the 2in figure. Without it the three cylinders give Cd = 1.14, 1.15 and 1.16. Those differences are smaller than the run-to-run scatter (±0.03), so they can't be told apart. Overall Cd = 1.15 ± 0.03.
- **Re now uses the actual water temperature** (your TODO). Assuming 20 °C had overstated Re by 6–17%, so Re now runs from 4.7×10³ to 5.0×10⁴.
- **New result: Strouhal number.** The ripple in the drag trace comes from vortex shedding. Its frequency gives St = 0.200 for every run, varying by less than 0.001. That's the textbook value, but it's suspiciously tight for 5-second windows, so check it against the raw spectra.
- **Blockage correction** (your other TODO). A standard correction lowers Cd to 1.07, 1.05 and 1.02, with the biggest change for the 2in cylinder. It's comparable to the scatter, so whether you headline corrected or uncorrected values matters. That's your call, and I've marked it as a TODO.
- **Runs scatter more than measurement noise explains.** The run-to-run variation is 2–3× the within-run uncertainty, so something differs between runs (speed repeatability, leftover waves from the previous run, etc.). Repeat runs would settle this.
- The October plot with Cd ≈ 0.98 is fully explained by the earlier length of 0.7 m instead of 0.6 m, so it's superseded.

**What I changed:**
- Merged `process.py` and `process_b3.py` into one `process.py` (your TODO). It reads data from this folder rather than the Dropbox path. It also takes each sensitivity from its calibration file rather than a hard-coded number.
- Added `analyze.py`, which writes `results/`, the Cd/St vs Re figure, and the table and numbers used in the paper.
- Updated `plot_timeseries.py` for the paper, and added matplotlib and scipy to `requirements.txt`.
- The paper builds in Docker, since you don't have LaTeX installed locally.
- `process_b3.py`, `forces_b3.csv` and `analysis.ipynb` are now superseded. I left them in place for you to delete when you're happy.

**Before you circulate it:**
- **Authors and apparatus:** the TODOs cover authors, the motivation paragraph, apparatus details (load cell model, carriage speed accuracy, cylinder finish and mounting), and systematic uncertainties.
- **Choice of journal:** I used a generic article format. If you go with *Experiments in Fluids*, it would need moving to Springer's template.
- **References:** verify every bibliography entry. They're standard works, but I wrote the citation details from memory and didn't look them up.

`calkit init` made this folder a git repository, but nothing is committed yet. I left that for you.
